title: Word Search
description:
# Word Search

Given an `m x n` grid of characters `board` and a string `word`, return `true` *if* `word` *exists in the grid*.

The word can be constructed from letters of sequentially adjacent cells, where adjacent cells are horizontally or vertically neighboring. The same letter cell may not be used more than once.

## Example 1:

**Input:** board = [["A","B","C","E"],["S","F","C","S"],["A","D","E","E"]], word = "ABCCED"
**Output:** true

## Example 2:

**Input:** board = [["A","B","C","E"],["S","F","C","S"],["A","D","E","E"]], word = "SEE"
**Output:** true

## Example 3:

**Input:** board = [["A","B","C","E"],["S","F","C","S"],["A","D","E","E"]], word = "ABCB"
**Output:** false

## Constraints:

*   `m == board.length`
*   `n = board[i].length`
*   `1 <= m, n <= 6`
*   `1 <= word.length <= 15`
*   `board` and `word` consists of only lowercase and uppercase English letters.

**Follow up:** Could you use search pruning to make your solution faster with a larger `board`?

solutions.name: Backtracking DFS
solutions.timeComplexity: O(m * n * 4^L) where L = word length
solutions.description: Try starting DFS from every cell. At each step, check bounds, character match, and visited status. Mark cell visited by modifying it, then restore after recursion.

solutions.name: Backtracking with Frequency Pruning
solutions.timeComplexity: O(m * n * 4^L) where L = word length
solutions.description: Before searching, count character frequencies in the board and verify the word can be formed. Also, reverse the word if its last character is rarer than its first to reduce branching. Use a separate visited array instead of modifying the board.

tests.description: Single cell board, single char word
Word uses all cells in 2x2 board
